draft.title: Vectors in motion
card: Displacement and velocity
Displacement is a vector for change in position. Velocity is a vector for the rate of change of position. With constant velocity v, displacement = v × t.
Relative velocity
The velocity of A relative to B is v(A) − v(B). Example: a boat moves at 5i + 2j and a current moves at 1i + 2j. The boat relative to the current is 4i + 0j.
Forces in balance
Forces are vectors. When forces are in balance, their sum is the zero vector. Example: 3i + 2j and −3i + 1j need a third force 0i − 3j to balance.
Constant force
A constant force F on mass m gives constant acceleration a = F ÷ m. Example: F = 6i + 12j with m = 3 gives a = 2i + 4j.
draft.remember: Subtract velocities for relative velocity. Balanced forces add to the zero vector. Acceleration = force ÷ mass.

a.q: Three forces act on a object at rest: 4i + 1j, −1i + 3j and F. They are in balance. What is F?
a.why: Balance means 4i + 1j + (−1i + 3j) + F = 0. The first two add to 3i + 4j, so F = −3i − 4j. The option 3i + 4j is the sum of the two forces, which forgets that F must cancel it.
a.clue: The three forces must add to the zero vector.

b.q: Car P has velocity 20i + 5j and car Q has velocity 12i + 9j, in km/h. What is the velocity of P relative to Q?
b.why: Relative velocity of P to Q = v(P) − v(Q) = (20 − 12)i + (5 − 9)j = 8i − 4j. The option −8i + 4j is the velocity of Q relative to P, which subtracts in the wrong order.
b.clue: Take the velocity of Q away from the velocity of P.

final.title: Vectors in motion
card: Displacement and velocity
Displacement is a vector for change in position. Velocity is a vector for the rate of change of position. With constant velocity \(v\), displacement \(= v \times t\).
Relative velocity
The velocity of \(A\) relative to \(B\) is \(v(A) - v(B)\). Example: a boat moves at \(5i + 2j\) and a current moves at \(1i + 2j\). The boat relative to the current is \(4i + 0j\).
Forces in balance
Forces are vectors. When forces are in balance, their sum is the zero vector. Example: \(3i + 2j\) and \(-3i + 1j\) need a third force \(0i - 3j\) to balance.
Constant force
A constant force \(F\) on mass \(m\) gives constant acceleration \(a = F \div m\). Example: \(F = 6i + 12j\) with \(m = 3\) gives \(a = 2i + 4j\).
final.remember: Subtract velocities for relative velocity. Balanced forces add to the zero vector. Acceleration \(=\) force \(\div\) mass.

a.q: Three forces act on an object at rest: \(4i + 1j\), \(-1i + 3j\) and \(F\). They are in balance. What is \(F\)?
a.why: Balance means \(4i + 1j + (-1i + 3j) + F = 0\). The first two add to \(3i + 4j\), so \(F = -3i - 4j\). The option \(3i + 4j\) is the sum of the two forces, which forgets that \(F\) must cancel it.
a.clue: The three forces must add to the zero vector.

b.q: Car \(P\) has velocity \(20i + 5j\) and car \(Q\) has velocity \(12i + 9j\), in km/h. What is the velocity of \(P\) relative to \(Q\)?
b.why: Relative velocity of \(P\) to \(Q\) \(= v(P) - v(Q)\) \(= (20 - 12)i + (5 - 9)j\) \(= 8i - 4j\). The option \(-8i + 4j\) is the velocity of \(Q\) relative to \(P\), which subtracts in the wrong order.
b.clue: Take the velocity of \(Q\) away from the velocity of \(P\).
